task.situation:
The parents’ association is preparing a meeting with the school management about young people and online advertising. It has asked your class to write a report on a survey you carried out among 200 students aged 14 to 18 at your school (the figures are invented for this task as a simplified example). The questionnaire also had a comment box. Survey results:
• average number of adverts counted during 30 minutes of scrolling on social media: 27
• students who follow at least one influencer who posts sponsored content: 82%
• students who can always or usually tell when a post is sponsored: 38%
• students who bought a product after seeing it in an online advert or sponsored post (last three months): 57%
• students who bought something because an influencer recommended it (last three months): 31%
• students who believe that online advertising does not influence them: 71%
task.instruction: Write a report for the parents’ association and the school management in which you:
points: present the main findings of the survey
assess the effects of online advertising on young people
recommend measures to help students deal with online advertising

words.short: Divide your report into sections and give them headings. Write around 250 words.
words.long: Divide your report into sections and give them headings. Write around 400 words.

task.de: Report an Elternverein und Schulleitung über eine für die Aufgabe erfundene Umfrage unter 200 Schüler:innen zu Online-Werbung. Drei Inhaltspunkte: Ergebnisse präsentieren, Auswirkungen auf Jugendliche beurteilen, Maßnahmen empfehlen (z. B. Medienkompetenz). Abschnitte mit Zwischenüberschriften, formell, keine Kurzformen.

meta.to: The Parents’ Association and the School Management

focus.label: data phrases
focus.note: Marked: phrases that present, describe, compare and interpret survey results (according to the survey, on average, more than four out of five, almost a third, the majority of, the results suggest that, it is striking that …). Numbers on their own and general linking words are not marked.

gaps.q: Our media project needs a catchy name. What do we call it?
gaps.qDe: Unser Medienprojekt braucht einen griffigen englischen Namen. Wie soll es heißen?

steps.q: Which subject line do we put in the header?
steps.de: Die Betreffzeile nennt das Thema des Reports.
steps.own: Short and factual: what is the report about?
steps.ownDe: Kurz und sachlich: Worum geht es im Report?

options.label: Survey plus purpose
options.text: Online advertising survey: results and recommendations
options.why: Factual and complete: it names the data and tells the readers that recommendations follow.

options.label: Topic first
options.text: Young people and online advertising: survey findings
options.why: Starts with the topic the parents care about and stays factual.

options.label: A clear focus
options.text: Adverts in students’ social media feeds: a survey report
options.why: Precise: it says where the adverts are and what kind of document this is.

steps.q: How do we open the report?
steps.de: Die Einleitung stellt den Report und die Umfrage vor. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete the introduction: who took part in the survey and what does the report do?
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Einleitung fertigschreiben: Wer wurde befragt, und wozu dient der Report?

options.label: State the purpose
options.text:
### Introduction
{{The purpose of this report is to present}} the results of a survey on online advertising {{carried out among}} 200 students aged 14 to 18. {{It also assesses}} the effects on young people and makes recommendations.
options.why: Purpose, data source and structure in clear sentences: a classic report opening.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
{{The purpose of this report is to present}} the results of a survey on online advertising {{carried out among}} 200 students aged 14 to 18. {{It also assesses}} the effects on young people and makes recommendations. {{The questionnaire asked}} about the adverts students see and the products they buy, and it ended with a box for personal comments.

options.label: Start with the problem
options.text:
### Introduction
In our opinion, online advertising has a strong influence on students, and we think that this is a problem. We feel that parents and the school should know about it, so our class asked 200 students about the adverts they see.
options.reject: ‘In our opinion’, ‘we think’ and ‘we feel’ turn the introduction into a comment. A report is impersonal: it states purpose and data source, not the writers’ opinions.
options.rejectDe: „In our opinion“, „we think“, „we feel“: Ein Report ist unpersönlich und nennt Zweck und Datenquelle, nicht die Meinung der Schreibenden.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
In our opinion, online advertising has a strong influence on students, and we think that this is a problem. We feel that parents and the school should know about it, so our class asked 200 students aged 14 to 18 about the adverts they see and the products they buy. We are sure that many parents will be surprised by the results.

options.label: Refer to the request
options.text:
### Introduction
{{At the request of the parents’ association, this report}} summarises the findings of our survey on online advertising, {{in which}} 200 students aged 14 to 18 answered questions about the adverts they see and the products they buy.
options.why: Names who asked for the report and describes the survey precisely.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
{{At the request of the parents’ association, this report}} summarises the findings of our survey on online advertising, {{in which}} 200 students aged 14 to 18 answered questions about the adverts they see and the products they buy. {{Only one school took part,}} so the results cannot be generalised, but they give a clear picture of how much advertising students here come across every day.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then complete the introduction: who took part, how the data was collected and what the report does.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Einleitung fertigschreiben: wer befragt wurde, wie die Daten gesammelt wurden und wozu der Report dient.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1 (content point 1): what are the main findings of the survey?
steps.de: Der erste Hauptteil präsentiert die wichtigsten Zahlen der Umfrage. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add the missing figures from the survey in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die fehlenden Zahlen aus der Umfrage mit eigenen Worten ergänzen.

options.label: Figure by figure
options.text:
### Main findings
{{[[According to the survey]], students [[counted an average of]]}} 27 adverts in 30 minutes, [[almost one a minute]]. {{[[More than four out of five]]}} follow an influencer who posts sponsored content, {{but [[fewer than two in five]]}} can usually recognise a sponsored post. {{In the last three months, [[more than half]]}} (57 per cent) have bought a product after seeing it advertised online. {{[[Surprisingly]], [[seven in ten]]}} believe that advertising does not influence them.
options.why: Every figure comes with a phrase that makes it easy to imagine: almost one a minute, four out of five.
options.textLong:
### Main findings
{{[[According to the survey]], students [[counted an average of]]}} 27 adverts in 30 minutes of scrolling, [[almost one a minute]]. {{[[More than four out of five]]}} follow an influencer who posts sponsored content, {{but [[fewer than two in five]]}} can usually recognise a sponsored post. {{In the last three months, [[more than half]]}} (57 per cent) have bought a product after seeing it advertised online, and [[almost a third]] on an influencer’s recommendation. {{[[Surprisingly]], [[seven in ten]]}} believe that advertising does not influence them. {{One comment sums up the feeling of many:}} “The adverts always know what I searched for yesterday.”

options.label: Start with the main finding
options.text:
### Main findings
{{[[According to the results]], adverts are}} part of students’ daily lives: respondents counted 27 [[on average]] in 30 minutes, and 82 per cent follow an influencer who posts sponsored content. {{[[It is striking that]] [[only a minority]]}} (38 per cent) can usually tell when a post is paid for. {{[[Perhaps the most surprising result]] is that [[seven in ten]]}} feel uninfluenced by adverts, even though [[more than half]] have recently bought an advertised product.
options.why: A topic sentence sums up the findings first, then the figures prove it, ending with the most surprising result.
options.textLong:
### Main findings
{{[[According to the results]], adverts are}} part of students’ daily lives: respondents counted 27 [[on average]] in 30 minutes, and 82 per cent follow an influencer who posts sponsored content. {{[[It is striking that]] [[only a minority]]}} (38 per cent) can usually tell when a post is paid for. {{[[Perhaps the most surprising result]] is that [[seven in ten]]}} feel uninfluenced by adverts, even though [[more than half]] have recently bought an advertised product and [[almost a third]] something an influencer recommended. {{Two concerns came up repeatedly in the comments:}} adverts that interrupt videos and games, and adverts based on students’ search history.

options.label: Report the figures
options.text:
### Main findings
The survey shows, that students see in average 27 adverts in 30 minutes of scrolling, which is almost one advert every minute. Most students follows influencers who post sponsored content (82 per cent). However, only 38 per cent can always or usually recognise a sponsored post. More than half (57 per cent) have bought a product after seeing an online advert, and 31 per cent have bought something because an influencer recommended it. Still, 71 per cent think that advertising does not influence them.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘shows, that’ (→ shows that: no comma before ‘that’), ‘in average’ (→ on average) and ‘follows’ (→ follow, because ‘students’ is plural).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: kein Beistrich vor that (shows that), in average → on average, follows → follow (Plural).
options.textLong:
### Main findings
The survey shows, that students see in average 27 adverts in 30 minutes of scrolling, which is almost one advert every minute. Most students follows influencers who post sponsored content (82 per cent). However, only 38 per cent can always or usually recognise a sponsored post. More than half (57 per cent) have bought a product after seeing an online advert, and 31 per cent have bought something because an influencer recommended it. Still, 71 per cent think that advertising does not influence them. In the comment box, several students wrote that the adverts they see are based on their search history.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add the missing figures in your own words and a comment that a student might have written (invent it).
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die fehlenden Zahlen mit eigenen Worten ergänzen und einen erfundenen Kommentar, den jemand an der Schule geschrieben haben könnte.

steps.q: Body paragraph 2 (content point 2): what effects does online advertising have on young people?
steps.de: Der zweite Hauptteil beurteilt, wie Online-Werbung auf Jugendliche wirkt. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain the effect in your own words and give an example.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Auswirkung mit eigenen Worten erklären und ein Beispiel geben.

options.label: Effects in everyday life
options.text:
### Effects on young people
This has a clear effect on them. Since they see them so often, they start to trust them, even when they have been paid for it. They then buy what they recommend, and it can add up quickly. As most of them do not notice this, it is hard for them to resist it.
options.reject: Who are ‘they’ and ‘them’, and what are ‘it’ and ‘this’? The reference words point back to nothing clear, so the reader cannot follow. Name the noun first.
options.rejectDe: Wer ist „they“/„them“, was ist „it“/„this“? Die Verweiswörter beziehen sich auf nichts Klares. Zuerst das Nomen nennen.
options.textLong:
### Effects on young people
This has a clear effect on them. Since they see them so often, they start to trust them, even when they have been paid for it. They then buy what they recommend, and it can add up quickly. Some of them even feel that they have to own it to belong, which can make them unhappy when they cannot afford it. This happens every day, so it shapes what they want and how they spend it. As most of them do not notice this, it is hard for them to resist it.

options.label: Hard to tell apart
options.text:
### Effects on young people
{{For many students, [[the figures suggest,]] the line between}} advertising and honest opinion is becoming blurred. {{Since [[the majority]] cannot reliably recognise sponsored posts,}} they may trust a recommendation that has been paid for. {{This is problematic because}} influencers often seem like friends rather than salespeople, and their advice feels personal.
options.why: Draws a clear conclusion from the 38 per cent figure and explains why it matters.
options.textLong:
### Effects on young people
{{For many students, [[the figures suggest,]] the line between}} advertising and honest opinion is becoming blurred. {{Since [[the majority]] cannot reliably recognise sponsored posts,}} they may trust a recommendation that has been paid for. {{This is problematic because}} influencers often seem like friends rather than salespeople. {{The danger is greatest for}} the [[more than two thirds]] {{who believe that adverts do not affect them,}} as they are less likely to question what they see, which makes them easier targets for clever marketing. {{In other words,}} the feeling of being in control may itself be part of the problem.

options.label: Spending money
options.text:
### Effects on young people
{{One clear effect, [[as the buying figures show]], is that}} adverts succeed in turning many young people into customers. {{Since one click is enough to order a product,}} pocket money can disappear within minutes, sometimes on items that soon end up unused in a drawer. {{Over a school year,}} such small purchases can add up to a large sum.
options.why: Links the effect to the buying figures and explains how one-click shopping makes spending easy.
options.textLong:
### Effects on young people
{{One clear effect, [[as the buying figures show]], is that}} adverts succeed in turning many young people into customers. {{Since one click is enough to order a product,}} pocket money can disappear within minutes, sometimes on items that soon end up unused in a drawer. {{Influencers add social pressure to spend:}} when they present new trainers or headphones as a must-have, {{young people may feel that}} they have to buy them to belong. {{Over a school year,}} such purchases can add up to a large sum, {{which can lead to}} frustration when the money is gone.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then explain the effects in your own words, give an example and say why they matter.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Auswirkungen mit eigenen Worten erklären, ein Beispiel geben und sagen, warum sie wichtig sind.

steps.q: Body paragraph 3 (content point 3): what do we recommend to the school?
steps.de: Der dritte Hauptteil leitet aus den Ergebnissen Empfehlungen an die Schule ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete the recommendation with your own ideas.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Empfehlung mit eigenen Ideen ergänzen.

options.label: Media literacy lessons
options.text:
### Recommendations
{{Given these effects, it is recommended that}} media literacy become part of lessons for 14- and 15-year-olds, with a focus on recognising sponsored content and understanding how targeted adverts work. {{These lessons could end with a poster campaign called ‘{PROJECT}’,}} in which students show others how to identify hidden adverts.
options.why: Links back to the effects; a long-term measure in lessons and a visible campaign.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
{{Given these effects, it is recommended that}} media literacy become part of lessons for 14- and 15-year-olds, with a focus on recognising sponsored content and understanding how targeted adverts work. {{These lessons could end with a poster campaign called ‘{PROJECT}’,}} in which students show others how to identify hidden adverts. {{Parents could support this work at home,}} for example by looking at a sponsored post together with their children and discussing who paid for it and why, or by agreeing on spending limits for app stores and online shops.

options.label: Students teach students
options.text:
### Recommendations
{{With these risks in mind, it is recommended that}} older students run {{a peer project called ‘{PROJECT}’, in which they show younger students how to}} recognise paid posts. {{Given that}} young people often listen to peers more than to adults, this approach should work, and the older students would learn a lot themselves.
options.why: Links back to the effects and uses the fact that teenagers listen to each other.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
{{With these risks in mind, it is recommended that}} older students run {{a peer project called ‘{PROJECT}’, in which they show younger students how to}} recognise paid posts. {{Given that}} young people often listen to peers more than to adults, this approach should work, and the older students would learn a lot themselves. {{Parents could take part as well:}} at a parents’ evening, the peer team might show them how sponsored posts are marked and suggest questions they could ask their children about the adverts in their feeds.

options.label: A project for everyone
options.text:
### Recommendations
It is recommended that the school do something about online advertising, as the survey shows that it is a real problem. A project called ‘{PROJECT}’ could deal with the topic in some way, and everybody should try to be more careful online in future. Teachers could also mention the topic in their lessons at some point.
options.reject: This sounds like a recommendation, but it names no real measure: ‘do something’, ‘in some way’ and ‘at some point’ tell the school nothing. Content point 3 needs concrete steps: who does what, for whom and how.
options.rejectDe: Klingt nach Empfehlung, nennt aber keine echte Maßnahme: „do something“, „in some way“, „at some point“. Gefragt sind konkrete Schritte: wer, was, für wen, wie.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
It is recommended that the school do something about online advertising, as the survey shows that it is a real problem. A project called ‘{PROJECT}’ could deal with the topic in some way, and everybody should try to be more careful online in future. Teachers could also mention the topic in their lessons at some point, and parents should play their part as well. If everyone works together, the situation will certainly improve, and students will be better prepared for the future.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then complete the recommendations with your own ideas for the school and for parents.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Empfehlungen mit eigenen Ideen für die Schule und für Eltern ergänzen.

steps.q: How do we end the report?
steps.de: Der Schluss greift Ergebnisse, Auswirkungen und Empfehlungen auf und rundet den Report ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete both sentences in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann beide Sätze mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben.

options.label: Sum up the main finding
options.text:
### Conclusion
{{To sum up, [[the findings demonstrate that]]}} online advertising influences students more than they realise: many buy advertised products, but only 38 per cent can spot a sponsored post. {{If these recommendations are put into practice,}} young people can become more critical consumers.
options.why: Repeats the key finding, picks up the effects and links them to the recommendations.
options.textLong:
### Conclusion
{{To sum up, [[the findings demonstrate that]]}} online advertising influences students more than they realise. Adverts fill their feeds, many respondents buy advertised products, and only 38 per cent can spot a sponsored post. {{This leaves them open to}} persuasion that they hardly notice. {{If these recommendations are put into practice,}} young people can become more critical consumers who make their own choices.

options.label: A skill to learn
options.text:
### Conclusion
{{Overall, [[the results show that]]}} recognising advertising is a skill that many students still lack, even though adverts fill their feeds every day. {{With the measures recommended above,}} our school could help students make their own decisions online.
options.why: Turns the findings into a clear message and ends with the purpose of the report.
options.textLong:
### Conclusion
{{Overall, [[the results show that]]}} recognising advertising is a skill that many students still lack, even though adverts appear in their feeds almost every minute and often lead to purchases. {{Like any other skill, it can be learnt.}} {{With the measures recommended above,}} the school and parents could help students make their own decisions online and spend their money more carefully.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then sum up the findings, the effects and the recommendations in your own words.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Ergebnisse, Auswirkungen und Empfehlungen mit eigenen Worten zusammenfassen.

checks.en: Header complete: To, From, Date and a factual subject line
Five sections, each with a clear subheading
The introduction states the purpose and who took part in the survey
All figures are taken correctly from the survey
All three content points: findings, effects, recommendations
Formal and impersonal: no contractions, no personal feelings

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen Report auf B1+/B2-Niveau nach SRDP-Muster zu einer Umfrage über Online-Werbung und übt dabei, Umfrageergebnisse präzise zu beschreiben, Auswirkungen zu beurteilen und Maßnahmen formell zu empfehlen.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen, Beamer im Vollbild. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige. Die Umfrageergebnisse aus der Aufgabe zusätzlich an die Tafel schreiben oder als Balkendiagramm austeilen. Vorab den Wortschatz klären: sponsored content, influencer, targeted, media literacy. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5 min pro Abschnitt, in der langen Fassung 8–9 min.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: rechts oben das Datum, als Überschrift „Report“ (wie am Beamer). Darunter der Kopf wie am Beamer: To, From, Date, Subject (die Betreffzeile wird im ersten Schritt gewählt). Fünf Abschnitte (Introduction, Main findings, Effects on young people, Recommendations, Conclusion): jeder beginnt mit seiner Zwischenüberschrift auf einer eigenen Zeile (unterstrichen), am Rand steht nichts; darunter der Absatz, zwischen den Abschnitten eine Zeile frei. Wendungen für Daten (Data phrases) grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: 6 Entscheidungen: Betreffzeile und fünf Abschnitte. Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe und Ergebnisse lesen, 6 Entscheidungen à 2 min, ca. 25 min Abschreiben, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (100 min): dieselben Entscheidungen mit längeren Abschnitten (u. a. Kommentare aus der Umfrage, eine weitere Auswirkung, Empfehlungen auch für Eltern), ca. 45 min Abschreiben. Gerüst kurz (realistisch ca. 60 min): 4 min Aufgabe, pro Abschnitt 1 min Abstimmung, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben, 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; in einer 50-Minuten-Stunde den Schluss als Hausübung und die Checkliste am Beginn der nächsten Stunde. Gerüst lang (100 min): gleicher Ablauf, pro Abschnitt 8–9 min eigenes Schreiben. Die Umfrageergebnisse bleiben an der Tafel, weil die Zahlen in den eigenen Sätzen gebraucht werden.
teacher.traps: Introduction B (LSR): persönliche Meinung (In our opinion, we think, we feel) statt unpersönlichem Report-Stil, der Zweck und Datenquelle sachlich nennt. Main findings C (LSA): Beistrich vor that, in average, follows. Effects on young people A (CC): unklare Verweiswörter (they, them, it, this), die sich auf kein genanntes Nomen beziehen. Recommendations C (TA): keine konkrete Maßnahme („do something“, „in some way“, „at some point“). Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Der Report hat immer fünf Abschnitte (Einleitung, drei Hauptteile, Schluss). Die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen mit längeren Abschnitten: Kommentare aus der Umfrage, eine weitere Auswirkung und Empfehlungen auch für Eltern. Keine echten Influencer:innen bewerten, keine Körperbild-Themen, keine Kaufentscheidungen einzelner Schüler:innen besprechen. Die Umfrageergebnisse sind für die Aufgabe erfunden; als Einstieg kann die Lehrkraft 30 Sekunden durch einen neutralen Beispiel-Feed scrollen, die Klasse zählt die Werbung mit. Wer Zeit hat, ergänzt bei Effects on young people einen Satz mit „This is worrying because …“. Differenzierung: Schnelle ergänzen im Gerüst-Modus einen weiteren Vergleich (z. B. „more than half“, „almost a third“). Hausübung: den Report mit anderen Entscheidungen neu schreiben oder eine anonyme Mini-Umfrage in der Klasse auswerten.
